commit_message:
[Codegen][CPU] Add RISC-V V bf16 vfwmaccbf16 inner_tiled MMA. (#25120)

Lower MMA_RISCV_V_VFWMACCBF16_*_F32_BF16 to llvm.riscv.vfwmaccbf16
(+zvfbfwma). N is vlen/8. Reuses `lowerRiscvVFmaccLike`. The spacemit
X60 board I have does not advertise zvfbwma, so didn't collect
performance numbers. The other dtypes are being tracked here: #24932

Correctness: a 64x64 ones matmul matched exactly under QEMU 8.1.2
(vlen=256, x-zvfbfwma). Lit covers VLEN 128/256/512 and the narrow-N
tile.

Towards #24311 

Assisted-by: Cursor

commit_message:
[Codegen][CPU] Add RISC-V V bf16 vfwmaccbf16 inner_tiled MMA. (#25120)

Lower MMA_RISCV_V_VFWMACCBF16_*_F32_BF16 to llvm.riscv.vfwmaccbf16
(+zvfbfwma). N is vlen/8. Reuses `lowerRiscvVFmaccLike`. The spacemit
X60 board I have does not advertise zvfbwma, so didn't collect
performance numbers. The other dtypes are being tracked here: #24932

Correctness: a 64x64 ones matmul matched exactly under QEMU 8.1.2
(vlen=256, x-zvfbfwma). Lit covers VLEN 128/256/512 and the narrow-N
tile.

Towards #24311 

Assisted-by: Cursor

---------

commit_message:
[VM] Index bytecode debug database source maps by function ordinal

`DebugDatabaseBuilder::addFunctionSourceMap` placed each function source map at the `ordinal` attribute of the function and fell back to 0 when the attribute was absent. Since ordinals moved to `OrdinalAnalysis` the bytecode target no longer sets that attribute, so every function wrote slot 0 and the debug database kept only the map of the last function encoded. The runtime looks function names and locations up in that table by internal ordinal, which made `--trace_execution` and backtraces report the wrong function for ordinal 0 and a bare ordinal for the others.

The fallback dates from the introduction of the debug database in 2e711d471c. At the time the bytecode pipeline ran `OrdinalAllocationPass` and every function carried the attribute by serialisation, so the default never applied. The move to `OrdinalAnalysis` in aa776b3ea7 (#23115) dropped that pass from the bytecode pipeline and replaced the other ordinal reads of the target, which dereference the attribute and would have asserted. This one substituted 0 and went unnoticed, since no test covered the contents of the debug database.

The encoder already holds the `OrdinalAnalysis`, so it now passes the ordinal to the builder, and the builder no longer reads the attribute. A new lit test, `debug_database.mlir`, checks that each function of a module gets its own entry in `debug_database.functions`.

Fixes #25277

Signed-off-by: Hamid El Maazouz <hamid.elmaazouz@gmail.com>
